analysis.title: USA: FOMC Minutes Note "Most" Participants Saw Another Increase as Likely "Appropriate by Year End," but Committee Will Approach Each Meeting with an Open Mind
key_insights: The September FOMC minutes show "all" participants supported raising the target range for the federal funds rate by 25bp to 3.75-4%, as they had not seen "sufficient progress on lowering inflation in recent months."
"Almost all" participants judged risks to inflation as "tilted to the upside." Risks to the labor market had "diminished" and were now "broadly balanced."

"Several" participants described the pre-hike policy rate as "not restrictive or only mildly restrictive." "Many" called the hike "prudent on risk-management grounds" with inflation "persistently above target," while "a number" saw it as necessary under their modal outlook.

"Most" participants assessed that another increase would likely be "appropriate by year end." They also said they approach each meeting with "an open mind" and that decisions "would depend on incoming information."

Participants cited "ongoing geopolitical developments" and "surging AI-related investments" as sources of inflation pressure. "Several" said core goods inflation stayed elevated as AI buildout effects increased and tariff effects waned. "Some" warned the AI buildout could push aggregate demand above aggregate supply.

"A few" participants said software and portfolio management fees made outsized contributions to recent PCE readings, which would likely fade with the BEA's upcoming methodology changes. Medium- and longer-term inflation expectations were judged "consistent" with the 2% objective.

"A few" participants tied the rise in longer-term Treasury yields to a stronger economy, higher expected AI-related borrowing and geopolitical developments. "Many" judged financial conditions "supportive of economic growth," citing equity gains and narrow corporate spreads. GS sees the change in financial conditions as only a small drag on 2026 GDP growth and a modest weight on 2027 growth.

The staff's September inflation forecast was "somewhat higher" for 2026-2028 than in July, reaching 2% in 2029, with upside risks. The growth and labor outlook strengthened: real GDP was projected to outpace potential through 2028 and unemployment to stay below the staff's longer-run estimate through 2029.

GS expects the second Fed hike in December, after the August core PCE data incorporating BEA methodology changes and speeches by Vice Chair Jefferson and NY Fed President Williams. GS sees a strong chance the FOMC ultimately concludes further hikes are unnecessary.
